correctness.rationale: An explicit inversion from full-rank quadratic-affine spatial log measurements at two times proves injectivity for all physically admissible parameters. Every rank-deficient sensor geometry must be contained in a hyperplane or a sphere, where reflection or exact mass-diffusion inversion gives distinct parameters with all-time equal traces. One-time inverse degeneracy is also exhibited, and Python checks independently validate exact identities and 1,200 reconstructions (6,036 assertions). The infinite theorem is proved analytically, not inferred from tests.

value.rationale: This solves the physically motivated distinction between investing in more sensors and increasing observation frequency for a single pollutant impulse when diffusivity is unknown. The minimal d+2 spatial threshold and unavoidable full-trace circle/sphere ambiguity are structural and counterintuitive; they directly delimit design choices beyond calibrated-diffusivity literature. No downstream theorem is claimed, nor is the full atmospheric model idealized away without disclosure.
